About Me

I'm Alisha Pokharel, an international student from Nepal pursuing an MBA in Applied Business Analytics in the United States while supporting faculty research in Economics, Finance & Global Business. With a background in Computer Science and Cognitive Science, I enjoy connecting data, technology, and people to turn complex business problems into practical, human-centered solutions.

I'm especially interested in analytics, AI, and product strategy, with a long-term goal of helping build technology that is both intelligent and genuinely useful. Outside of work and academics, I enjoy traveling, exploring food and shopping, and cooking Nepali cuisine.

Beyond the résumé

My Journey

A personal note
“I do not think I became a completely different person. I think I became a clearer version of the person I already was.”

I grew up in Kathmandu, Nepal, with a strong desire to become independent in how I think, choose, speak, and build my life. Moving to the United States gave me new opportunities, but it also taught me how to adapt, make difficult decisions, and keep moving when the path was unfamiliar.

That journey changed how I approach problems today: I still care deeply about people and intuition, but I have learned to pair them with analysis, structure, curiosity, and reason.

01

Where I started

Kathmandu shaped my values: courage, kindness, independence, family, and the belief that fear should not make my decisions for me.

02

What changed me

Studying and living far from home taught me resilience, financial responsibility, self-reliance, and how to balance emotion with thoughtful analysis.

03

What I’m building toward

I want to use analytics, technology, and human-centered thinking to solve practical problems — while staying curious, useful to others, and grounded in where I came from.

Credit Risk Prediction & Decision Support App

Python · Machine Learning · Streamlit · Independent Study

Problem
Lending decisions require a consistent way to assess credit risk across financial and customer information.
Analysis
Analyzed 1,000 loan applications, prepared financial and customer data, and compared 4 predictive models to build a data-driven risk assessment workflow.
Insight
Identified key risk drivers, including loan duration, checking-account status, and credit amount.
Recommendation
Use the deployed Streamlit application to standardize risk evaluation with model-generated predictions and confidence scores.
Impact
Delivered an interactive decision-support tool that translates predictive modeling into clear, standardized outputs to support lending decisions.
PythonMachine LearningStreamlitCredit Risk

Scam or Safe: A Study of Students' Link-Clicking Behavior

Independent Honors Research · Aug 2025 – May 2026

Problem
Universities invest heavily in phishing-awareness training, but it's unclear whether students' confidence in spotting scams actually makes them safer.
Analysis
Designed and ran a Qualtrics-based experiment with 83 undergraduates, measuring phishing-detection accuracy, self-reported confidence, and response time.
Insight
Confidence predicted how fast students decided — not whether they were right.
Recommendation
Awareness training should calibrate confidence alongside detection skill, not just response speed.
Impact
Gives universities a research-backed basis for redesigning phishing-awareness programs.
Research DesignStatistical AnalysisQualtrics

Spotify Parental Control Strategy

Independent Product Case Study

Problem
Spotify's parental controls have a recurring, high-friction pain point showing up repeatedly in negative reviews.
Analysis
Analyzed 100+ user reviews and app-store feedback to identify and prioritize the biggest pain point.
Insight
One control gap accounted for a disproportionate share of complaints — a signal clear enough to act on directly.
Recommendation
Proposed a user-centered fix scoped to that specific gap and aligned with Spotify's existing product and business goals.
Impact
A targeted fix aimed at reducing support friction and negative reviews — without a full feature rebuild.

Full-Stack Web App (MERN) · 2 Team Members

Problem

ATM Software Engineering System

C++ · 4 Team Members

Problem
Banking software must be rigorously specified before a line of code is written, since transaction-logic errors carry real-world cost.
Analysis
Modeled a full ATM system with object-oriented design — 10+ UML use cases plus class and sequence diagrams — following formal SDLC practices with a 4-person team.
Insight
Rigorous upfront modeling surfaced edge cases, like failed transactions and concurrent access, before implementation instead of after.
Recommendation
Apply the same design-before-code discipline to any system where failure is costly or hard to reverse.
Impact
Produced a documented, implementation-ready system design — the artifact a bank would need before funding a build.
C++UMLSDLC
Documentation →

AI-Assisted Network Optimization

3 Team Members

Problem
Network routing bottlenecks are hard to spot analytically until traffic is modeled at scale.
Analysis
Simulated real-world internet routing networks using graph theory with a 3-person team, applying AI-assisted methods to analyze bottleneck patterns.
Insight
Graph-theoretic simulation made bottleneck patterns visible that weren't obvious from raw traffic data alone.
Recommendation
Extend the simulation approach to test proposed routing changes before deploying them on real infrastructure.
Impact
Gives network operators a lower-risk way to test capacity and routing decisions before touching production infrastructure.
Graph TheoryData Analysis

Course Search App

UI/UX Design · 2 Team Members

Problem
Students struggle to discover and plan courses efficiently within existing academic-planning tools.
Analysis
Conducted user research with 50+ students and applied usability principles to design a mobile academic-planning tool in Figma, with a 2-person team.
Insight
Discovery, not scheduling, was where students lost the most time — validated directly through the research with 50+ students.
Recommendation
Prioritize a discovery-first flow — search, filter, recommendation — ahead of deeper scheduling features.
Impact
A validated, research-backed design direction ready to hand off for build — lowering the risk of building the wrong thing first.
